articles.title: Baby Found in Critical Condition After Social Services Closed Case
articles.excerpt: A 19-month-old girl was taken to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, according to a safeguarding review in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
A 19-month-old girl was taken to hospital in critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, a Child Safeguarding Practice Review has found. The girl weighed 9.7lb (4.4kg) when she was treated in February 2025, less than half the expected weight of 24lb (11kg) for her age.

The review reported that the girl was severely dehydrated, covered in sores, and had "paper-thin skin". Experts noted that she displayed skin breakdown across her bottom and nappy area, with open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom.

The case was closed despite warnings that her mother, who was 17 when the baby was born, was neglecting her daughter and had avoided contact with social workers and health visitors for weeks. Rochdale Borough's Safeguarding Children Partnership accepted the findings of the review and stated it was taking action.

Expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall highlighted that medics found "wasting to the buttocks" and described the girl's condition as "incredibly emaciated".

articles.title: Rochdale Veteran Seeks Justice Following Nuclear Tests
articles.excerpt: John Morris, a Rochdale veteran exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s, expresses renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Andy Burnham as Prime Minister.
articles.content_html:
A man from Rochdale who was exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s has expressed renewed hope for justice following the appointment of Andy Burnham as Prime Minister. John Morris, now 88, was 18 when he participated in tests at Christmas Island in the Pacific Ocean, where bombs were detonated as part of a series of Ministry of Defence (MoD) operations.

Morris is among a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the MoD, claiming they have been denied justice. Many veterans have reported serious health issues as a result of their exposure during the tests and are calling for an independent inquiry into the matter. Burnham has previously supported their cause, stating that there is clear evidence of misconduct in public office.

In 2025, while serving as mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham indicated that the investigation into the veterans' claims could not be delayed any longer. Morris believes that Burnham's support could lead to a judicial review, which he sees as a significant step forward for veterans seeking accountability.

The MoD has stated that compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme, but many veterans feel this is insufficient. Morris's comments reflect a growing frustration among those affected by the tests, as they continue to seek recognition and justice for their experiences.

articles.title: Fire Breaks Out in Smallbridge, Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A fire broke out in Smallbridge, Rochdale, on Friday evening, prompting a response from firefighters who worked through the night to extinguish the flames and monitor the aftermath.
articles.content_html:
A fire broke out in an open area on Spring Mill Walk in Smallbridge at around 8:15pm on Friday, July 24. Aerial images captured the impact of the fire, which burned overnight and produced large plumes of black smoke visible across Rochdale.

Firefighters worked throughout the night to extinguish the flames and remained on the scene until around 1pm on Saturday, damping down hotspots and monitoring the aftermath. Dramatic photos on social media showed the extent of the fire, which involved a large quantity of waste at the site.

Officials from the Environment Agency were called in, and the local council was alerted due to the nature of the incident. Pictures taken by a drone camera later revealed a significant area of scorched earth and debris left behind by the fire.

No injuries have been reported as a result of the fire. Fire crews are expected to continue monitoring the site in the coming days.
